name: Aichi D3A2 Model 22 Val
blurb: A fixed-gear carrier dive bomber with two 7.7 mm cowl guns and, in Dev only, one belly bomb rack. Its speed and climb come from one Allied intelligence sheet, and its stall speed, roll rate and handling are estimates; the drawn model's variant is unconfirmed.
history:
The Aichi D3A, the Navy Type 99 Carrier Bomber, was the Imperial Japanese Navy's primary dive bomber of the war, with an elliptical wing and fixed landing gear; the Allies called it "Val". It entered service in 1940 and flew from many of the Navy's carriers, Akagi, Kaga, Shokaku and Zuikaku among them.

It took part in almost every Navy action of the war, from Pearl Harbor and the first strikes on U.S. bases in the Philippines onward, and it sank more Allied warships than any other Axis aircraft.

What this entry models: the Model 22 figures (span, weight, engine ratings, top speed, climb) come from a single Allied intelligence sheet of December 1944, which disagrees with other published figures (for example 267 mph at 20,300 ft against the sheet's 281 mph). The stall speeds, roll rate, dive limit and control feel are estimates scaled from the Zero, and the undercarriage is fixed: the gear key does nothing, and a landing is always on the wheels. The rear gunner's gun is not modeled. The bomb offered in Dev is the Hellcat's 1,000 lb store on one belly rack, standing in for a historic load of one 550 lb bomb and two 130 lb bombs. The drawn model may be a different variant from the one flown.

sources.title: Val 22, TAIC Manual No. 1 sheets 401A-2 and 401A-3, December 1944 (Japanese Aircraft Performance and Characteristics, archive.org)
